title: Large GTA 6 footage uploads are now resumable
summary: YTIntel hardens the Creator Assets foundation for the kind of files it is actually meant to hold. Gameplay files above 6 MB now use resumable TUS uploads through Supabase's direct Storage hostname with chunk progress, retry/resume support, pause/resume controls and automatic media metadata capture. Creator DNA is physically outside Analyse in Vault, and the installed PWA no longer exposes a stale Compare shortcut.
discord_changes: 🎥 LARGE GAMEPLAY UPLOADS: Creator Assets now switches files over 6 MB to resumable TUS uploads instead of relying on one fragile request.
⏯️ RESUME + PROGRESS: 6 MB chunks, automatic retry, interrupted-upload resume, live percentage, pause/resume controls and a leave-page warning protect long GTA 6 captures.
🧾 BETTER FOOTAGE RECEIPTS: uploaded videos now bank detected duration, dimensions, resolution and upload protocol alongside rights + attribution metadata.
🧹 PRODUCT CLEANUP: Creator DNA now physically lives in Vault, and the installed PWA's obsolete Compare shortcut / Group Analysis copy is removed.
changes: Added v376-resumable-creator-assets.js as a focused large-file upload layer on top of the existing private Creator Assets cloud library.
Files above 6 MB are routed through Supabase Storage's resumable TUS endpoint using the direct project Storage hostname and fixed 6 MB chunks.

Interrupted uploads can reuse the previous TUS upload URL; a stable per-file pending path is retained until successful completion so retries resume the correct object rather than creating mismatched metadata.
Added live byte/percentage progress, pause/resume controls, retry delays and a before-unload guard while an upload is active.
Added local media probing before banking: duration, width, height and inferred resolution are saved with the Creator Assets record when the browser can read them.
Extended Creator Assets event semantics in Supabase so resumable uploads can be logged as uploaded instead of being mislabeled as shared.
Moved the Creator DNA card out of Analyse in the static document and into Vault, removing reliance on post-boot DOM relocation for the intended information architecture.
Removed the stale Compare Winners PWA shortcut and Group Analysis wording from the installed app manifest; the PWA now exposes Analyse, Creator Assets + Vault and Watchtower.
Advanced the app shell/service-worker cache to v0.37.6 and added a dedicated regression test for resumable uploads, Creator DNA placement and Compare absence.
Preserved the v0.37.5 private per-user storage/RLS foundation and the v0.37.3 single-video Analyse focus.
known_limitations: The upload pipeline stores original files; automatic transcoding, proxy generation, thumbnail extraction, scene splitting, embeddings and creator-facing CDN delivery are still future milestones.
Actual maximum file size is still governed by the Supabase project's global and bucket Storage limits; YTIntel does not attempt to bypass those limits.
TUS resume metadata is browser-local, so resuming an interrupted upload is strongest when retried from the same browser/device.
Creator referral records and asset event logging exist, but anonymous click attribution, creator dashboards, affiliate payouts and fraud-resistant conversion accounting are not complete yet.

Publisher/platform rights still govern gameplay redistribution. YTIntel does not treat self-recording as automatic permission to sublicense footage; public commercial licence copy must be verified game-by-game before rollout.
YouTube does not expose a reliable Most Replayed curve for every video. Missing replay evidence remains missing rather than fabricated.
Public storyboard sprites are sampled seek-bar evidence rather than every encoded frame. Exact encoded-frame-by-frame semantic analysis remains an active Endgame workstream.
Waveform-level silence/transient analysis requires a directly decodable public audio stream; semantic music/SFX labels additionally require supported source metadata or local audio intelligence.
why_it_matters: The footage product only works if creators can bank hours of high-resolution gameplay without a single network wobble wasting the whole upload. v0.37.6 makes that foundation materially more credible while also cleaning up two product-regression issues: Creator DNA being structurally inside Analyse and Compare still surviving in the installed PWA.
